title: CS-led feasibility spark and impact-slicing canvas for enterprise asks
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success receive a steady stream of enterprise feature asks that are framed as discrete asks but vary wildly in value, complexity, and regulatory sensitivity. Current first-pass scoping is inconsistent across account reps and often lacks an engineering feasibility signal, causing lengthy back-and-forths and inflated expectation setting.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'Feasibility Spark' workshop + an 'Impact-Slicing Canvas' artifact that CS can run asynchronously or in a 30-45 minute sync with PM/Eng presence to produce a score-backed intake card. Output should give a triage verdict: Quick Win, Needs Design Spike, Multi-sprint Project, or Decline.

Scope:
- Design a one-pager Impact-Slicing Canvas with four axes: Customer Value, Implementation Runway (engineering time + infra risk), Compliance/Privacy Sensitivity, and Strategic Alignment.
- A short scoring rubric (0-5) and guidance for CS to gather minimal evidence (example asks, affected endpoints, data classifications, SLA required).
- A template output to be written into Linear (fields, suggested labels, estimated size band).
- A facilitation playbook for CS to run a 30-45m Feasibility Spark with required attendees and decision rules.
- A follow-up flow: when to open a Design Spike, how to tag as 'Needs Legal Review', and when to create a Dedicated Capacity evaluation.

Out of scope: detailed design specs, implementation plans, or long-running discovery projects (those become Design Spikes).

Why this matters: Reduces time-to-decision on enterprise asks, standardizes CS signals for product/eng, and prevents mis-scoped promises during sales cycles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deliver Impact-Slicing Canvas one-pager (PDF + Google Slide).
- Create a 2-page CS playbook with script and decision rules.
- Linear intake template created and documented (fields auto-fill guidance).
- Trial 6 Feasibility Sparks across CS reps and record outcomes; at least 4/6 produce an actionable triage card.
- Engineering and Legal sign-off on scoring rubric for compliance sensitivity categories.
decisions:
- Use 0-5 scoring per axis to produce a 0-20 normalization score.
- Score buckets: 0-6 = Decline or Do Later, 7-12 = Design Spike required, 13-16 = Potential Multi-sprint Project (requires PM prioritization), 17-20 = Quick Win / Fast-track.
- For any compliance score >=4, auto-add label 'needs-legal' and route to Security.
- For implementation runway score >=4, suggest creating Eng Spike with 5-day allocation for feasibility assessment.
